fighters.name: Красный Пухляш
fighters.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a production-oriented transparent sprite animation atlas for Clay Fight, a children's app demonstrating how kids can sculpt their own plasticine creatures and make stop-motion fighters.
Create ONE sprite sheet of ONE ORIGINAL friendly little monster repeated in exactly 16 frames, arranged in an exact 4 columns x 4 rows grid of equally sized invisible square cells. Requested canvas 2048x2048. No grid lines and no labels. This is an animation asset, not a poster or character lineup.
STYLE: an actual little plasticine craft made by a 6-8 year old child, photographed frame by frame for a stop-motion cartoon. Charming clumsy hand-rolled balls, squashed blobs and short sausage limbs, visible fresh fingerprints and thumb smudges, obvious pressed-on eyes and belly pieces, slightly uneven left-right shapes. Soft fresh vivid colored clay, friendly comic monster appeal like the warm playful creature world of Monsters Inc, but original creature designs. Very simple forms a child could sculpt at home. Big expressive eyes, cute round body, short plump limbs, soft silly expressions, broad rounded feet. No defined muscles, no realistic human anatomy, no ferocious angry brows, no frightening teeth, no dirty cracked aged clay, no fur, no clothing, no armor, no glossy CGI/vinyl or polished toy look.
COMPOSITION INVARIANTS: exact same character identity, colors, proportions, number of eyes and horns and limbs in every frame. Every body is full length inside its own cell, with feet anchored to the same local baseline at 86% cell height, same fixed camera and scale, same soft lighting upper left. Full figure at about 64% of the cell height, enough empty margins for extension of arms/legs. Three-quarter SIDE view facing RIGHT in every frame. Character root remains horizontally centered in every cell; only pose changes. Each row read left to right is a distinct four-frame stop-motion action.
ROW 1 punch sequence: frame 1 playful ready stance; frame 2 draw forward arm back to wind up; frame 3 visibly extend that fist horizontally RIGHT in a light cartoon jab, slight torso lean right; frame 4 recoil arm back to ready stance.
ROW 2 kick sequence: frame 1 playful ready stance; frame 2 bend and lift the front knee; frame 3 extend front foot RIGHT for a funny low kick while balancing on rear foot; frame 4 bring foot down and return to ready stance. Keep grounded foot on baseline.
ROW 3 block sequence: frame 1 playful ready stance; frame 2 raise both arms toward face; frame 3 clearly cross forearms in front of face and lean slightly back in a defensive block; frame 4 lower arms to ready stance. For crab arms use crossed closed pincers.
ROW 4 pain/hit reaction sequence: frame 1 normal ready stance; frame 2 eyes squeeze shut and body squashes in a small surprised recoil; frame 3 lean back LEFT with arms flung slightly apart, mouth in a small funny O as if saying 'oops'; frame 4 recover toward the ready stance with a sheepish smile. Mild slapstick only. No injury, blood, bruises, tears, impact symbols, opponent or effects.
BACKGROUND: genuine transparent alpha throughout empty space and cell gutters; no ground plane, no cast shadows outside figures, no background color, no paper, no checkerboard pattern. No text, names, numbering, logos, panel borders, dividers, watermarks or UI.
CHARACTER: A tomato-red dumpling-shaped little monster with a big pear-shaped head and belly merged into one blob, a small orange oval belly patch, TWO big off-white clay eyes with black dot pupils, no nose, a small friendly curved mouth, two short red sausage arms ending in rounded red mitten hands, two very short legs and wide red oval feet. No horns, no human face, no gloves. Slightly different eye sizes, endearing and funny. Childish rather than muscular, simple 7-9 blobs of plasticine.
